clue.text: Has the ability to deal somehow with supporting structure for bust lighting

parts.note: can means is able to, has the ability to

indicators.note: somehow means in some way or other, so the letters of deal are rearranged

parts.note: a bra is the garment that supports the bust

explanation.surface: Someone manages to handle the scaffolding needed to light a sculpted bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' suggests a sculpture of a head, but the supporting structure for it is a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabra is a branched holder for several candles or lamps, an item of lighting.

clue.text: Satellite absorbing negative energy is all one colour

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the adjective

indicators.note: something absorbing another takes it inside itself

parts.note: the Moon is Earth's satellite
not is the word of negation
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A satellite photo absorbing negative energy shows nothing but a single hue.
explanation.walkthrough: The negative sits inside the moon, then E for energy is tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotone describes something of a single tone or shade without variation.

clue.text: Large woman's crime?

parts.note: large means big
Amy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An offence committed by a big woman, the question seems to ask.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the crime is not about size at all: a big name for a woman plus her name builds the offence of marrying twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy, marrying while already married, is a criminal offence in many countries.

clue.text: Keen to upset drama queen

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, and in a down entry that reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: keen means eager, avid

explanation.surface: Someone eager to annoy a theatrical, attention-seeking person.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a temperamental star, and the term is used for any self-important prima donna.

clue.text: Willingness to cooperate with new mates before rescheduled trip around island

indicators.note: before in a down clue means placed above, so the first jumble comes ahead of the rest
new here means made afresh, so the letters of mates are rearranged
around tells us the rearranged trip goes round the island letter
rescheduled means put into a new arrangement, so the letters of trip are reordered

explanation.surface: Friends show willingness to work together before a holiday to an island is moved.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate anagrams here, each with its own indicator, and the second one also holds the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit is the feeling of loyalty and cooperation among members of a group, a willingness to pull together.

clue.text: African woman captivating Scandinavians

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the woman's name holds the other piece inside

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name
Danes are Scandinavians, people of Denmark

explanation.surface: An African woman charming a group of Nordic men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African woman' reads as one phrase, but African alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudanese means from Sudan, a country in north-east Africa, and also names its people.

clue.text: Hunts under cover for pieces of plants

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the stems that hold leaves or flowers

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests foraging in undergrowth; the two halves are separate meanings, a verb and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To stalk is to track stealthily, while stalks are the slender stems of plants.

clue.text: God of love turning up in pain

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: in pain means sore

explanation.surface: Cupid's counterpart arriving to cause heartache.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek deity of desire, the equivalent of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Sailor visiting poor region around Irrawaddy's source finds indigenous inhabitant

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor; visiting just has him arrive first, ahead of the rest

indicators.note: around tells us the jumbled region goes round the letter from the river
poor means in bad shape, so the letters of region are rearranged
a river's source is where it begins, so the first letter of Irrawaddy is taken

parts.note: the Irrawaddy is the main river of Myanmar

explanation.surface: A sailor travels up a river in a poor region and meets a local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source' suits a river, so it gives the first letter of Irrawaddy, which the anagram of REGION goes around.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is one of the original inhabitants of a land, an indigenous person.

clue.text: Speak of lead-free dairy product

indicators.note: free of its lead means losing its first letter

parts.note: butter is made from cream

explanation.surface: Talking about a dairy item that contains no lead.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead-free sounds like unleaded petrol or paint; here the lead is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say aloud or voice words, a synonym of speak.

clue.text: Play containing one old 3-D scene

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the play word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a drama is a play
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A theatre production contains an old three-dimensional set.
explanation.walkthrough: The two single letters go in after the first letter of DRAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model of a scene, often in a museum display case.

clue.text: Setter playing the part of man with disease

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
an actor plays as a character
Les is a man's name

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter acting a role of a man who is ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Measles is a contagious viral illness marked by a red rash.

clue.text: Potty in toilet nearly emptied

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: emptied means hollowed out, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A child's potty sitting in a toilet that's almost empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' looks like a child's toilet seat to match 'toilet'; it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Potty and loony are both informal British words for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Blue prepared to retain record

indicators.note: retaining something means keeping it held inside

parts.note: food is dressed when prepared for serving
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A sad person ready to keep an old disc close.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling sad or low, which is what depressed means.

clue.text: Dash for a curry, say, getting scoffed outside front of restaurant

indicators.note: getting adds the next piece directly after the first

parts.note: a curry is an example of a dish

indicators.note: outside says the word for scoffed goes around the selected letter

parts.note: scoffed means eaten greedily

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of restaurant

explanation.surface: Rushing out for a curry and wolfing it down outside the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' reads as a quick trip out; it is the verb meaning to crush someone's hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash someone's hopes is to dishearten them, making them lose spirit.

clue.text: Immoral character entered age falsely

indicators.note: falsely means wrongly, so the letters are put down in the wrong order

parts.note: the ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked person lied about their age on a form.
explanation.definitionFit: A degenerate is a person whose morals have declined to a corrupt level.

clue.text: Sincere gent gets bras undone for women's medical examination

indicators.note: undone means unfastened and taken apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A well-meaning man unhooks bras during a check-up for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Breast screening is the routine mammogram check offered to women to detect cancer early.

clue.text: Worried, if priest's in aeroplane!

indicators.note: worried means agitated and shaken about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous cleric finds himself up in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is' and joins the anagram to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spitfire was a famous British fighter aircraft of the Second World War.

clue.text: Buried together with revolutionary

parts.note: the prefix inter- means together or mutually, as in interconnect
red is a common label for a revolutionary or communist

explanation.surface: Laid in the grave alongside a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury a body, so interred is a past tense of buried.

clue.text: Bow tie refashioned by court designer

indicators.note: by means beside, so the court letters come next to the rest

parts.note: an arch is a bow, a curved structure

indicators.note: refashioned means made into a new shape, so the letters of tie are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bow tie remade by a court tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow tie' reads as one item of neckwear, but 'Bow' is the curve and only 'tie' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An architect designs buildings, so is a designer: a specific example of the general word.

clue.text: Shed tears about a female at last — sneaky!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for shedding tears goes round the other letters

parts.note: to cry is to shed tears

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of the word at

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone weeps over a woman at the end, which is a cunning move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' sounds like 'finally', but it gives the last letter of 'at'; with A and F it sits inside CRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning and deceitful, which is what sneaky means: an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Vanquished, beheaded and consumed

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: vanquished means defeated, beaten

explanation.surface: A grisly fate: defeated, decapitated and devoured.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten and consumed both describe food that has been taken in.

clue.text: Small company used recycled Portuguese money once

indicators.note: recycled means processed into a new form, so these letters are remade

parts.note: CO is the short form of company
taken as written

explanation.surface: A small firm reused old Portuguese coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' signals an abbreviation of company, not a size.
explanation.definitionFit: The escudo was Portugal's currency before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Why punishment?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a severe telling-off, as in to give someone this

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a child's protest; the second sense is the British idiom 'give someone what for', a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: 'What for?' asks a reason, and in British idiom giving someone what for means punishing or scolding them.

clue.text: Listened to music in cloak

indicators.note: listened to means heard rather than read, so a word's sound is wanted

parts.note: rap is a style of music

explanation.surface: Someone heard songs while wearing a cape.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap is a loose garment worn around the shoulders, like a shawl or cloak.

clue.text: Dog adopted by fortune-teller is less likely to suffer harm

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so the dog goes inside

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A dog taken in by a clairvoyant is safer now.
explanation.definitionFit: Securer is the comparative of secure, meaning safer from danger.

clue.text: Little sister, clutching Pimms, initially drinks delicately

indicators.note: clutching means holding tightly, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: sis is a short form of sister

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: first letter of Pimms

explanation.surface: A younger sibling holds a glass of Pimm's and drinks it daintily.
explanation.walkthrough: Pimm's is a British gin-based summer drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To sip is to drink in small mouthfuls, delicately.

clue.text: Post a newspaper to the Queen

parts.note: taken as written
FT is the Financial Times
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Mailing a newspaper to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like a verb for mailing; it is the Latin prefix post-, meaning later.
explanation.definitionFit: Post as in postwar means later in time, the sense of after.

clue.text: Wise to sulk about Enid dancing with former partner?

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the name Enid is rearranged
with joins the last piece onto the rest

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
the four letters of Enid rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it sensible to brood over Enid dancing with your ex?
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a pet' is an old phrase for in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedient means advisable or prudent in the circumstances, a sense close to wise.
